# bugs #4253: mcs51 --xstack: a branch on the char result of a call tests the register that is restored last from the external stack

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/4253/
- Category: [Fixes](../../fix.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17228
- Recommended action: Apply the patch and close. It also fixes #4254. Its tests need the patch for local 0020, without which --xstack does not link.
- Patch: [bugs-4253.patch](../../patches/bugs-4253.patch), commit [`4c9b047ed`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/4c9b047edfdf3a026a7da04af30a2db0901614bc). Applies to r17228 without the other patches.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

With `--xstack`, the code for a call whose 8-bit result is tested moves the result to A, and then
it restores the registers that were in use at the call from the external stack. It reads each
register through A, and the conditional jump after the restore tests the value of the register
that was restored last. The ticket's `first()` returns 1, and 2 is correct.

This was reproduced on r17193 in ucsim. The result is 1 with `--model-large --stack-auto --xstack`,
`--model-small --stack-auto --xstack`, `--model-large --xstack`, and
`--model-large --stack-auto --xstack --opt-code-size`. It is 2 with `--model-large --stack-auto`,
`--model-large`, and `--model-small`. The `--xstack` programs were linked with the library of the
model without `--xstack`, and the linker warns about conflicting options. On r17228, programs with
`--xstack` link only with the patch for local 0020, and the tests under Verification show the
fault there.

## Cause

`genCall` in `src/mcs51/gen.c` assigns the result of the call and then calls `unsaveRegisters`.
With `--xstack`, `unsaveRegisters` reads each register from the external stack through A. With
`--opt-code-size` and two or more registers, it calls `sdcc_xpop_regs`, which takes a count and a
register mask in A and B. `genCall` has code that pushes A before `unsaveRegisters`, and pops it
after, when `--xstack` is in effect and its variable `accuse` is true.
[r14433](https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/code/14433/) set `accuse` to
`IC_RESULT (ic)->aop->regs[A_IDX] > 0`. For each register, `regs[]` has the index of the byte of
the operand that the register holds, or -1. When the result is in A, or in A and B, A holds byte
0, so `accuse` is false, and `genCall` does not push A. Before r14433, `accuse` was the return
value of `assignResultValue`, which reported whether A is in use after the assignment. `genCall`
does not push B, before r14433 or after it.

## Fix

With the patch, `genCall` sets `accuse` when `regs[A_IDX]` is 0 or more. It also pushes B before
`unsaveRegisters` and pops it after, when the result has a byte in B, `--xstack` is in effect, and
`optimize.codeSize` is set. Only the restore with `sdcc_xpop_regs` writes B. With
`--opt-code-size` and exactly one register to restore, `unsaveRegisters` does not call
`sdcc_xpop_regs`, and the `push b` and `pop b` are 4 bytes that the code does not need.

`accuse` has a second use, which does not depend on `--xstack`. When it is true, `genCall` emits
`push acc` before the three instructions that remove more than 3 bytes of arguments from the
stack, and `pop acc` after them. `packRegsForAccUse` in `src/mcs51/ralloc.c` keeps the result of a
call out of A when the callee is reentrant and has the flag `FUNC_HASSTACKPARM`, which a C23
function that is declared `(...)` does not have. The entry local 0017 describes that fault.
Without the patch, the jump after a call of such a function with more than 3 bytes of arguments
tests the value of the stack pointer. With the patch, `pop acc` reads an argument byte, and the
jump tests that byte.

## Verification

`support/regression/tests/bug-4253.c` has the ticket's function, a function with the call in the
condition of a loop, and a function with several registers in use at the call. That function is
compiled a second time after `#pragma opt_code_size`, so that `sdcc_xpop_regs` restores the
registers. `bug-4254.c` is the test for #4254. Of the regression variants, `mcs51-xstack-auto`
alone passes `--xstack`, together with `--stack-auto` and the small model.

Without the patch, on r17228 with the earlier patches of this report, `bug-4253` fails its 6
assertions and `bug-4254` fails 6 of its 12 for `mcs51-xstack-auto`, and both pass for
mcs51-small, mcs51-large, and stm8. These runs had the libraries of the build with all patches.
With the patches of this report on r17228, both tests pass for `mcs51-xstack-auto`. The regression
suite has 0 failures for host, stm8, ucz80, and six mcs51 variants: the four models, and
`--stack-auto` with the small and large models. The diagnostics suite has 0 failures for mcs51,
mcs51-large, mcs51-stack-auto, z80, and stm8. On the nine regression targets, the size of every
other test is equal with and without the patch.

The whole suite was run twice for `mcs51-xstack-auto` on r17228, each time with the library that
the compiler of the run built. One run has the patches of this report, and the other does not
have the patches for #4253, local 0014, #4118, and #3357. 80 tests fail without them and 64 with
them, and every test that passes without them also passes with them. The 16 tests that fail only
without them are `dynamic`, `arraybounds`, `bug-1292721`, `bug-3985`, `bug-4047`, `cse`, `ctype`,
and `string`, and the gcc-torture tests 20000910-2, 20020529-1, 20050502-1, divcmp-3, pr20100-1,
pr66233, pr87290, and strlen-3. `compound-literal-eval` has 2 failures in place of 3. Apart from
`inline`, whose source the patch for #3357 changes, 41 tests are larger with the patches, by 421
bytes in total. On r17200, the code of `atof`, `isalnum`, `ispunct`, `strdup`, and `time` in the
xstack library differed with the patch, so a library that is built without the patch has the
fault in these functions.

## Related

- #4254 reports the fault for an int result, where the restore also overwrites B. This patch
  fixes it.
- The entry local 0016 describes another fault with `--xstack`, in which the restore of one
  register overwrites a result in r0. It is present with and without the patch.
- The entry local 0017 describes the fault of functions that are declared `(...)`, which the
  second paragraph of Fix mentions.
- The entry local 0020 has the patch that programs with `--xstack` need to link on r17228.
